text:
maria: heads up — customer X on our private appliance reported NVidia driver mismatch after kernel patch last week. pods failing with NCCL init errors. 

ops-bot: [automated] alert created: incident/driver-drift-1752504321 (severity: medium)

maria: logs look like 
```
E1123 14:01:12.345 NCCL ERROR init : Unhandled CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN on gpu 0
CUDA driver version: 470.129.6, required: 510.x
```

tj: ugh. is this on-prem only or also in our dedicated fleet?

maria: so far customer-reported only on their VPC gateway + one private rack we manage. Dedicated in-cloud seems fine — same model/containers but different host kernel + driver bundle.

sophie: what does the supported matrix say? I thought we certified 470/11.x kernels for older cards.

ryan: our matrix: CUDA 11.4 / driver 470 for T4s, CUDA 11.7 / driver 510 for A10s+. But customers sometimes run mismatched host drivers. Private deployments expect us to run the driver installer, but some customers pin host drivers for other infra reasons.

customer-eng: FYI the customer said they upgraded their host kernel to 5.19 for a security patch, then started seeing failures. They claim they didn't touch drivers.

tj: kernel bump can break driver ABI if distro package wasn't rebuilt. Could be DKMS missing. We should ask for `nvidia-smi -a` and `modinfo nvidia` output.

maria: asked for outputs. Also found one hint: their `/lib/modules/5.19.0-.../kernel/drivers/net/` contains out-of-tree module that keeps `nvidia` from binding properly.

sophie: two threads here: 1) immediate workaround for customer, 2) longer-term policy so private installs don't drift under us. For workaround: we can push a fallback model variant that uses lower NCCL version? Risky.

ryan: fallback to CPU is also possible as emergency, but will kill latency and cost. For inference-critical customers we need faster fix. If we can coordinate a driver reinstall (matching 510.x) that should restore NCCL.

maria: customer is hesitant to let us change host drivers. They want a supported matrix clarification first. They're arguing our docs only list a single driver per GPU family, not kernel compat notes.

tj: docs are ambiguous. We need to add kernel compatibility rows and call out DKMS / distro package requirements. Also add an explicit "minimum host OS patch level" for each driver bundle.

customer-eng: also ask them if they use vendor kernels (e.g., Oracle UEK) or custom grub args. Those often cause module signature enforcement.

ops-bot: [action] assign @tj to create matrix PR, due EOD tomorrow.

tj: will do. also proposing we add a preflight check to private deploy CLI that verifies host driver/kernel combo and flags probable drift. It can read /proc/driver/nvidia/version and compare to our pinned bundle.

sophie: +1 to preflight. Also propose we ship a lightweight agent for Managed Private that reports host driver, kernel, and last upgrade time (opt-in). Would save repeated tickets.

ryan: cost note — if we mandate driver roll for on-prem and offer installation support, that's professional services time. Need to surface in sales quotes.

maria: for the customer now: they allowed a reboot into previous kernel while we continue troubleshooting. I'll escalate if `nvidia-smi` still shows mismatch after boot.

tj: in parallel I'll open a compatibility matrix PR with: supported driver versions, supported kernels (major.minor), DKMS requirement, known-disallowed distros, and recommended `modprobe` checks. Link it here when ready.

customer-eng: customer appreciated the revert option. tagging @sophie for matrix / doc language since they'll likely push back on wide policy.

sophie: I'll draft the doc with examples and two templates: "Managed Private" (we can change host) and "Customer-Managed" (we provide verifier & instructions).

maria: perfect. follow-up: if any of you see the `NCCL graph mismatch` errors too, paste them here. Might be a kernel-level netdev ordering issue we've not seen before.

ryan: will loop infra sales on PS pricing.

maria: thanks all — tracking in incident/driver-drift-1752504321. Closing thread when matrix PR merged. :thumbsup:
